messages.subject: lognormal clarification
parts:
Hello all,

I have a quick clarification question. The manual's discussion of changes of variables and manually adjusting the log probability uses the example of a log normal distribution parameterized as log(y) ~ normal(mu, sigma). However, a footnote on pg. 149 recommends using the lognormal probability function instead, as in: y ~ lognormal(mu, sigma). Is it also necessary to increment the log probability manually when using the lognormal function?

Devin

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] lognormal clarification
parts:
On 1/25/14, 2:51 AM, Devin Caughey wrote:
> Hello all,
>
> I have a quick clarification question. The manual's discussion of changes of variables and manually adjusting the log
> probability uses the example of a log normal distribution parameterized as log(y) ~ normal(mu, sigma). However, a
> footnote on pg. 149 recommends using the lognormal probability function instead, as in: y ~ lognormal(mu, sigma). Is it
> also necessary to increment the log probability manually when using the lognormal function?

No. The only time you need to do a Jacobian adjustment
is when the left-hand side of a "~" involves parameters to which
you've applied a non-linear change of variables.

If y is a parameter or transformed parameter or local variable that
depends on a parameter, then you need it with

log(y) ~ normal(mu, sigma);

If y is just data or transformed data, you don't need the adjustment.

Also, you never need an adjustment with

y ~ lognormal(mu,sigma);

if y is a parameter.

- Bob
